reference: GNU Bash's kill -l builtin, which independently maps signal names and numbers; Bash's type/help builtins for the documented loadable metadata. No signal is delivered by any runnable fixture.
coverage: Bash builtin type and synopsis metadata for the loadable
Named, prefixed, numeric, and automatic-direction signal lookups against GNU Bash kill -l
Dynamic RTMIN/RTMAX endpoint and adjacent realtime-name round trips
Known-signal table listing derived from GNU Bash numeric lookups
Unknown name and out-of-range number errors
Deferred end-to-end delivery to an owned child only
exclusions: No fixture sends a signal, signals a process group, or interacts with a host/system process.
Cross-libc signal numbering is not covered; parity uses GNU Bash and the candidate in the same isolated environment.
Deferred owned-child delivery and trap/wait integration is not claimed as passed.

cases.purpose: Bash type reports the loadable under its documented command name as a builtin.
Bash help metadata contains the documented list, name-to-number, and number-to-name forms.
cases.script: doc=$(help signal); [[ $doc == *'signal -l'* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *'signal -n NAME'* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *'signal -s NUMBER'* ]] || exit 1; [[ $doc == *'NAME-OR-NUMBER'* ]] || exit 1; printf 'documented-usage-present\n'

cases.purpose: The -n option maps a conventional name and a SIG-prefixed name to GNU Bash's signal numbers.
cases.script: if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then signal -n TERM; signal -n SIGUSR1; else kill -l TERM; kill -l SIGUSR1; fi

cases.purpose: The -s option maps ordinary signal numbers to GNU Bash's canonical names.
cases.script: if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then signal -s 15; signal -s 10; else kill -l 15; kill -l 10; fi

cases.purpose: A bare name resolves to its number and a bare decimal number resolves to its canonical name.
cases.script: for value in TERM 15; do if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then signal "$value"; else kill -l "$value"; fi; done

cases.purpose: RTMIN, RTMAX, and their adjacent names round-trip through numbers using the runtime's GNU Bash signal table.
cases.script: if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then min=$(signal -n RTMIN); max=$(signal -n RTMAX); min1=$(signal -n RTMIN+1); max1=$(signal -n RTMAX-1); signal -s "$min"; signal -s "$max"; signal -s "$min1"; signal -s "$max1"; else min=$(kill -l RTMIN); max=$(kill -l RTMAX); min1=$(kill -l RTMIN+1); max1=$(kill -l RTMAX-1); kill -l "$min"; kill -l "$max"; kill -l "$min1"; kill -l "$max1"; fi

cases.purpose: Compare signal -l's number/name rows with an independent table generated by GNU Bash kill -l for each valid number; empty reserved slots and intermediate realtime aliases are omitted because signal -l documents only named signals and the RT endpoints.
cases.script: if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then signal -l; else for number in {1..128}; do if name=$(kill -l "$number" 2>/dev/null); then if [[ -n $name ]]; then case "$name" in RTMIN+*|RTMIN-*|RTMAX+*|RTMAX-*) continue ;; esac; printf '%2d %s\n' "$number" "$name"; fi; fi; done; fi

cases.purpose: GNU Bash recognizes Linux signal 16 as STKFLT; this checks whether the loadable accepts the same name without delivering the signal.
cases.script: if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then signal -n STKFLT; else kill -l STKFLT; fi

cases.purpose: Unknown names and out-of-range numbers fail without producing lookup output; command statuses are recorded so a mismatch remains visible even though the fixture itself completes normally.
cases.script: if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then if signal -n NOT_A_SIGNAL >/dev/null; then name_status=0; else name_status=$?; fi; if signal -s 999 >/dev/null; then number_status=0; else number_status=$?; fi; else if kill -l NOT_A_SIGNAL >/dev/null; then name_status=0; else name_status=$?; fi; if kill -l 999 >/dev/null; then number_status=0; else number_status=$?; fi; fi; printf '%s %s\n' "$name_status" "$number_status"

cases.purpose: Future integration coverage should pass a looked-up name or number to a signal-delivery path and verify handler, wait status, and disposition behavior.
cases.reason: The current suite is limited to pure lookups and must not deliver signals. A future test requires a disposable VM or an independently reviewed syscall mock that creates one directly owned child, records the requested signal and resulting handler/wait status, proves an unrelated sibling is untouched, and prevents any target outside the fixture-owned PID set.

cases.purpose: Linux signal aliases resolve to the same number as the canonical name in the independent Bash table; no signal is sent.
cases.script: for pair in IOT:ABRT POLL:IO CLD:CHLD; do if type -t signal >/dev/null 2>&1; then signal -n "${pair%:*}"; else kill -l "${pair#*:}"; fi; done
